name: Technical Writing Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any technical writing task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any technical writing task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting technical writing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Keep technical writing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. Document any non-obvious technical writing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
4. When technical writing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
5. Prefer explicit, readable technical writing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
6. Validate technical writing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. Prefer the simplest technical writing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
8. Keep technical writing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
9. Measure before optimizing any technical writing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
10. State assumptions about technical writing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
11. When technical writing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated technical writing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop technical writing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new technical writing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting technical writing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these technical writing guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
